rendered: The document gives a strain-level verdict from the LDA of all tested strains. Fully discriminated: Five strains, including P. aeruginosa, E. coli,[1] E. sakazakii, L. monocytogenes, and E. faecium, were fully distinguishable[2]. Only partial discrimination: S. typhimurium and S. aureus, where the text says partial discrimination was achieved for S. typhimurium and S. aureus[3]. The concentration gradient itself was run only on a subset of strains. The text says that In the case of P. aeruginosa, E. coli,[4] E. sakazakii, and L. monocytogenes, the signal channels of the single-[5] probe showed consistent evolution with concentration. E. faecium, S. typhimurium and S. aureus were not part of that series, so the document does not say how they behaved across concentrations. In the concentration LDA plots (Fig. 3[6]), the concentration clusters are non-overlapping for P. aeruginosa, L. monocytogenes and E. coli. For E. sakazakii, the figure reading shows the highest-concentration clusters lying close together and partly overlapping, which is a caveat to the blanket 'fully distinguishable' verdict for that strain.
